quests.instruction: Choose the sentence that makes a claim, something a reader could agree or disagree with.
quests.prompt: A student is planning an essay about public parks. Which sentence is a claim?
options: The city has fourteen parks in total this year.
This essay is about public parks in our city.
Every neighbourhood should have a park nearby.
Some parks have playgrounds, ponds and picnic areas.
quests.hint: Ask which sentence would start a discussion, not end it.
quests.explanation: Only the first sentence takes a position that someone could challenge. The rest announce a topic or give facts that nobody would argue about.

quests.instruction: Which sentence could be the main claim of a short essay?
quests.prompt: A student is writing about learning new skills online.
options: Many videos teach guitar, cooking and coding today.
There are websites for learning new languages online.
Online courses can begin at any time of the year.
Learning a skill online is better than in a classroom.
quests.hint: A main claim states a position, not just what exists.
quests.explanation: The first sentence compares two ways of learning and takes a side. The alternatives describe what online learning offers, without saying whether it is better.

quests.instruction: Select the TWO sentences that make a claim someone could disagree with.
quests.prompt: Topic: public libraries.
options: Libraries are more valuable to a town than cinemas.
The main library has a reading room upstairs.
Most libraries lend books for two or three weeks.
Libraries should stop charging fees for late books.
quests.hint: Look for sentences where a reasonable person might say 'I'm not so sure'.
quests.explanation: 'More valuable' and 'should stop charging' are positions that people may disagree about. The loan period and the reading room are facts that can simply be checked.

quests.instruction: Choose the sentence that states the STRONGEST opinion.
quests.prompt: Four students give their views on a class trip to the science museum.
options: A trip to the science museum might be useful.
A trip to the science museum is essential for every student.
A trip to the science museum is fairly good for some classes.
A trip to the science museum could be quite interesting.
quests.hint: Compare how sure and how far-reaching each sentence sounds.
quests.explanation: 'Essential for every student' is the most certain and the widest claim. The other sentences use softer words such as 'might', 'could' and 'fairly'.

quests.instruction: Choose the sentence that gives a MILD opinion.
quests.prompt: A friend asks when you like to study.
options: I slightly prefer studying in the morning.
Nobody should study late at night.
Studying in the morning is the only sensible choice.
Morning is far better than any other time to study.
quests.hint: Which sentence leaves room for other views?
quests.explanation: 'Slightly prefer' is gentle and personal. The alternatives speak as if there were one correct answer, which is a much stronger stance.

quests.instruction: Choose the most cautious way to give an opinion.
quests.prompt: A manager asks for your honest but careful view of a new work schedule.
options: This schedule works perfectly for everybody.
This schedule seems to work well for most of the team.
This schedule will solve all our problems.
This schedule is the best decision we have made.
quests.hint: Careful wording avoids promising too much.
quests.explanation: 'Seems' and 'most of the team' limit the claim to what the writer can reasonably say. The other sentences promise perfect results for everyone.

quests.instruction: Choose the fact that best supports the opinion.
quests.prompt: Opinion: The city should add more lighting along the riverside path.
options: The path was completely repaved two years ago.
The river is about twelve kilometres long in total.
Many people enjoy walking beside the water at weekends.
Several runners tripped on the path after dark last winter.
quests.hint: Which fact shows a problem that lighting could solve?
quests.explanation: Trips in the dark are a real problem that lighting addresses. The river's length and the repaving date don't connect to visibility.

quests.instruction: Select the TWO facts that support the opinion.
quests.prompt: Opinion: Our hobby club should meet online instead of in person.
options: Members live in five towns, some over an hour away.
Online meetings can be joined from a phone or laptop.
The club room has an old piano in the far corner.
The club was formed by two teachers back in 2015.
quests.hint: Which facts make online meetings more practical?
quests.explanation: Travel time and easy access are facts that favour meeting online. The founding year and the piano say nothing about how the club should meet.

quests.instruction: Choose the fact that gives the strongest support.
quests.prompt: Opinion: Students should carry lighter school bags.
options: Most students carry a bag to school every single day.
The school day starts at 8:30 in the morning each day.
Nine students with heavy bags saw the nurse for back pain.
Bags come in many different sizes and colours.
quests.hint: The best fact links directly to the harm the opinion is trying to prevent.
quests.explanation: Back pain among students with heavy bags directly shows why lighter bags matter. The other facts are true but do not point to any problem.

quests.instruction: Choose the sentence that gives a personal experience as support.
quests.prompt: Opinion: Children should learn to swim early.
options: Swimming is a popular activity in many countries.
Some pools have shallow ends for young beginners.
Swimming is a very good form of exercise for adults.
When I fell into a pool at six, lessons kept me calm.
quests.hint: A personal example tells what happened to a real person.
quests.explanation: The first sentence tells a specific event that shows why early lessons mattered. The alternatives are general statements about swimming.

quests.instruction: Choose the personal example that best supports the opinion.
quests.prompt: Opinion: Public transport can save you money.
options: Buses and trains are used by many people every day.
A friend once told me that trains can be expensive.
Travel costs vary quite a lot from city to city.
Since I sold my car and bought a bus pass, I spend half as much.
quests.hint: Look for a real change or result that the writer actually experienced.
quests.explanation: The writer describes a change and its result in money terms. The other sentences are general, second-hand or uncertain.

quests.instruction: Select the TWO personal examples that support the opinion.
quests.prompt: Opinion: Working in a team can make projects easier.
options: Teams usually have more than two people in them.
In our robotics club, a teammate's coding covered what I could not do.
When three of us split the poster work, we finished early.
Some teachers prefer to give individual tasks instead.
quests.hint: Choose the sentences that describe something that happened to the writer.
quests.explanation: Both correct options describe real situations where teamwork helped. The other choices are general remarks that do not show teamwork making a project easier.

quests.instruction: Choose the reply that disagrees with the post.
quests.prompt: Sam posts: 'Coffee shops are great places to study.' Which reply disagrees?
options: True, and the cake is always a nice bonus.
I find them too noisy; a library works better for me.
Agreed, especially the ones that have free Wi-Fi.
Yes, and the background chatter helps me focus too.
quests.hint: Look for the reply that gives a different view of coffee shops as study places.
quests.explanation: The first reply says coffee shops don't work for the writer and offers a reason. The alternatives agree in different ways.

quests.instruction: Choose the reply that agrees AND gives a reason.
quests.prompt: Jo posts: 'Local shops deserve more support than online stores.'
options: Agreed, since money spent locally stays in our community.
Not really, because online prices are lower.
I disagree, but I can see your point.
Local shops are shops in the local area.
quests.hint: A good agreeing reply does more than say 'yes'.
quests.explanation: The right reply agrees and adds 'since money spent locally stays in our community'. One reply disagrees, one repeats the idea, and one is hesitant disagreement.

quests.instruction: Choose the reply that agrees only partly.
quests.prompt: A colleague writes: 'Remote work is better for everyone.'
options: No, working in an office is clearly the better choice.
Some people work remotely and other people do not.
Yes, it is the best option for the whole team here.
It suits many people, but not those needing a quiet workspace.
quests.hint: Partial agreement accepts one part of the claim and questions another.
quests.explanation: The first reply accepts that remote work helps many people, then points out a limit. The other choices agree completely, disagree completely, or say nothing about the claim.

quests.instruction: Decide who the message is most likely for.
quests.prompt: 'Hey! Did you see the new pizza place? Honestly, it's way better than the old one. We should go on Friday.'
options: A newspaper editor
A close friend
A company's customer service team
A school principal
quests.hint: Think about the informal tone and the invitation at the end.
quests.explanation: The casual language and the invitation show that the writer is talking to someone familiar. A principal, editor or customer service team would usually get more formal wording.

quests.instruction: Who is the writer most likely addressing?
quests.prompt: 'Dear Ms Adams, I would like to suggest that Year 8 students be allowed to use the library at lunchtime.'
options: A teacher or member of school staff
A friend from another school
A younger brother or sister
A crowd at a sports match
quests.hint: Notice the greeting and the way the request is made.
quests.explanation: 'Dear Ms Adams' and the polite suggestion show the writer is speaking to a school adult in a formal way.

quests.instruction: Choose the sentence that suits the audience.
quests.prompt: You are writing to your school principal to suggest a later start time.
options: Everyone knows that the current start time is a total joke.
Honestly, school starts way too early. It is crazy, and everyone knows it.
Start times are a topic that some people like to talk about.
I would like to suggest a later start, as many students arrive tired.
quests.hint: Consider the reader's position and choose a respectful tone that still states a position.
quests.explanation: This sentence is polite, clear and gives a reason. The first alternative is too casual, the second avoids taking a side, and the last is disrespectful.

quests.instruction: What is the writer's main purpose?
quests.prompt: 'The new phone plan charged me twice this month, and nobody has answered my emails. Please remove the extra charge.'
options: To complain and ask for action
To advertise the phone plan
To explain how phones work
To thank the company for its help
quests.hint: Ask what the writer wants to happen after the reader finishes.
quests.explanation: The writer describes a problem and requests a solution, which is a complaint. There is no advertising, no thanks and no explanation of technology.

quests.instruction: What is the purpose of this post?
quests.prompt: 'The trail to Green Lake is easy and beautiful. Go on a weekday and bring water.'
options: To warn people to avoid the trail
To ask for directions
To recommend the trail to other people
To report a news event
quests.hint: Look at the advice given at the end of the post.
quests.explanation: The writer praises the trail and gives tips for visiting, so the aim is to recommend it. There is no warning, news report or question.

quests.instruction: Choose the sentence that best matches the purpose of persuading a council.
quests.prompt: You want to persuade the town council to add a pedestrian crossing on Mill Lane.
options: The council should add a crossing on Mill Lane before someone is hurt.
Mill Lane is a two-lane road with a bus stop at each end.
Last Tuesday I walked along Mill Lane and took the bus home.
A pedestrian crossing is a marked place for people to cross.
quests.hint: Which sentence tries to make the reader act?
quests.explanation: Only the first sentence pushes the council toward a decision. The remaining options describe, narrate or define.

quests.instruction: Which sentence does NOT belong in the paragraph?
quests.prompt: Claim: The town needs a skate park. Sentences in the paragraph include the ones below.
options: Her brother bought new trainers last week.
It could also reduce skating on pavements.
A skate park would give them a safe space.
Teenagers have few places to meet.
quests.hint: Check which sentence has no link to the skate park idea.
quests.explanation: The trainers have nothing to do with the need for a skate park. The other three give reasons connected to teenagers and safety.

quests.instruction: Choose the sentence that should be deleted from the email.
quests.prompt: An employee is writing to a manager to argue for shorter Friday meetings.
options: Short meetings leave more time for real work.
Long meetings often repeat information from earlier emails.
Ending by 3 p.m. would help people with early train times.
I also think the coffee in the canteen should be cheaper.
quests.hint: One sentence introduces a second opinion that has nothing to do with meetings.
quests.explanation: The coffee comment is a separate issue, so it weakens the focus. The alternatives give reasons about time and meetings.

quests.instruction: Select the TWO sentences that drift away from the claim.
quests.prompt: Claim: Cats are easier pets than dogs for busy people.
options: Dogs have been companions to humans for thousands of years.
A cat can be left alone for a weekend with food and water.
Cats do not need to be walked several times a day.
Rabbits are also popular pets in small flats.
quests.hint: Only some sentences compare how much time each pet needs.
quests.explanation: The history of dogs and the popularity of rabbits do not help the comparison about busy people. The other two sentences address time and effort directly.

quests.instruction: Choose the word that completes the opinion best.
quests.prompt: 'The new app is very ____ because it saves me an hour of typing every week.'
options: useful
popular
colourful
modern
quests.hint: Choose the word that matches the reason after 'because'.
quests.explanation: Saving an hour of work makes the app useful. Popular, modern and colourful might describe it but do not follow from the reason.

quests.instruction: Choose the sentence that presents the opinion politely and with care.
quests.prompt: You want to tell a teammate that a deadline may be too short.
options: The deadline is a terrible mistake by management.
It seems to me the deadline is a little tight.
Anyone can see that the deadline is simply wrong.
The deadline is impossible for us to meet.
quests.hint: Polite opinions often soften the judgement instead of stating it bluntly.
quests.explanation: 'It seems to me' and 'a little tight' give the view without blaming anyone. The remaining options sound harsh or absolute.

quests.instruction: Select the TWO words that give a negative opinion of a product.
quests.prompt: Words from reviews of a pair of headphones.
options: adjustable
lightweight
overpriced
flimsy
quests.hint: Which words tell you the writer was disappointed?
quests.explanation: 'Flimsy' and 'overpriced' judge the product badly. 'Lightweight' and 'adjustable' describe features that most reviewers treat as neutral or positive.

quests.instruction: Choose the sentence that gives a clear opinion supported by a fact.
quests.prompt: Which sentence states an opinion and backs it with a relevant fact?
options: Cyclists need their own lane on Bridge Street after four accidents last year.
I think Bridge Street is fine just the way that it is now.
Bridge Street has a bridge, a bank and a bakery on it.
Cyclists are the friendliest people on the road, in my view.
quests.hint: Look for a sentence that includes both a position and evidence.
quests.explanation: The first sentence recommends a change and supports it with the number of accidents. The others give unrelated facts, an unsupported opinion, or an unrelated compliment.

quests.instruction: Select the THREE sentences that belong in a post supporting the idea. One does not belong.
quests.prompt: Claim: Our street should start a community garden.
options: The street was resurfaced in June.
Neighbours could share fresh vegetables.
The empty plot next to the bus stop is currently unused.
Children would learn how plants grow.
quests.hint: Which sentences give reasons or opportunities that connect to a garden?
quests.explanation: Shared produce, learning and a free plot are all connected to the garden idea. The resurfacing does not help the argument.

quests.instruction: Put the sentences in the best order for a short opinion text.
quests.prompt: Arrange these four sentences.
options: The notice on the door says it closes at 5 p.m., before most workers get home.
Opening until 8 p.m. would give them a real chance to use it.
Most people cannot visit while they are at work.
The library should stay open later on weekday evenings.
quests.hint: Begin with the claim and end with a sentence that connects back to it.
quests.explanation: The claim comes first, a reason follows, and a fact from the door notice gives evidence. The final sentence explains how the change would fix the problem.
